extracted.intended_audience: shippers and licensees of radioactive materials; device and packaging manufacturers; radiation safety officers; DOT/NRC regulators and policy stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Final-rule guidance and responses to public comments on revisions to the Hazardous Materials Regulations (HMR) and harmonization with IAEA standards affecting Type B/Specification packaging, transition periods, definitions, QA, and operational requirements for shipment of radioactive materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALARA consideration in remedial/alternative actions
rubrics_metrics.description: As low as reasonable achievable (ALARA) goal of minimizing occupational exposures to radiation should guide choices about operations such as source removal, setting up hot cells, or other refurbishment activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory and cost analyses must weigh occupational radiation exposure (ALARA) alongside feasibility and expense (e.g., portable hot cells are costly and increase occupational exposure). Alternatives that substantially increase dose are inconsistent with ALARA and should be disfavored even if technically feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic impact assessment on industry and small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate and justify industry-wide economic costs resulting from regulatory changes, including costs of design, testing and licensing of new designs; construction of new overpacks; loss of value of existing overpacks; and loss of value of existing devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide defensible numeric ranges (example provided: design/testing/licensing $3M–$7.8M; construction $2.5M–$5M; loss-of-value $1.5M–$3M; total $7M–$15.8M). Evaluate whether rule causes significant economic impact for a substantial number of small entities per the Regulatory Flexibility Act; quantify number of affected small-entity QA programs when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition period timing for phase-out of 1967 Specification packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt an effective five-year transition period from publication of the final rule: nine months from publication to effective date, then four years from the effective date before prohibited use of DOT 1967 Specification packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition period must be long enough to allow design, fabrication, testing, certification of new packages and orderly phase-out (addresses DOE remediation schedules, license termination, and international notification). A shorter period (e.g., two years) was judged insufficient; nine months + four years (≈5 years total) was adopted as reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for replacement packages to meet current safety standards and QA documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages replacing 1967 Specification packagings must be shown to conform to current safety standards and have appropriate quality assurance documentation; lack of QA documentation is an important reason to upgrade or replace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if design/procurement/construction standards may have been equivalent historically, without QA documentation equivalence cannot be assumed. Recertification or replacement is required unless equivalence to current requirements can be demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of DOT Specification 1967 packages (subject to transition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt elimination of DOT 1967 Specification packagings from domestic use for Type B quantities, with the specified transition schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although historical drop/fire/immersion tests were performed, many 1967 packages lack QA program elements and contemporary testing/stand-alone safety analyses; therefore elimination with transition is justified to increase transportation safety at reasonable cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and application of 'completely enclosed' for excepted packages (§173.424)
rubrics_metrics.description: Active material in an instrument or article intended for transport in an excepted package must be completely enclosed by the non-active components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Completely enclosed’ does not require air-tight enclosure. For example, Americium-241 smoke detectors qualify because the thin laminate and the positioning within the outer case provide sufficient retention even though the outer case is not air-tight. Clarify that enclosure can be achieved by combination of laminates/positioning that prevent escape under normal transport conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper shipping name and UN number usage during transition for Type B packages
rubrics_metrics.description: During the transition period, when Type B quantities are transported in 1967 DOT Specification packages or NRC-approved B( )/B( )F packages, permitted proper shipping names and UN numbers are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-fissile or fissile-excepted Type B quantity: use 'Radioactive material, Type B(U) package' and 'UN2916'. Fissile Type B quantity: use 'Radioactive material, Type B(U) package, fissile' and 'UN3328'. Include these explicitly in the final rule to remove ambiguity during the transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify 'consignment' definition for multimodal and bulk shipments
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify 'consignment' to meaningfully cover shipments in commerce, including bulk railcars, multiple railcars, intermodals, and distinctions between aircraft and rail shipments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a workable definition (e.g., ICAO/IATA formulation: one or more packages accepted by an operator from one shipper at one time and address, receipted for in one lot, moving to one consignee at one destination). Clarify whether a single railcar, multiple railcars, or multiple bulk containers constitute one consignment, and account for differing hazards across modes and load configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of 'wipe efficiency' in §173.443
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'wipe efficiency' for determining removable contamination so it is not confused with counting efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wipe efficiency should be defined as the fraction of removable contamination that is taken up by a wipe and counted as a sample (not the efficiency of the counting instrument). Insert parenthetical definition to eliminate longstanding confusion and misapplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training/instruction requirement for hazmat employees regarding regulatory changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Hazmat employees performing regulated functions must be instructed in new or revised function-specific requirements regardless of the three-year recurrent training cycle (HMR §172.702(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory changes relevant to a hazmat employee's functions require instruction as soon as the change affects their duties, independent of the periodic recurrent training schedule. Do not rely on waiting for the next three-year refresher to update employees on critical rule changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security/safeguard planning for devices that may become non-shippable
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess safeguard and security implications where devices/sources may become temporarily unshippable (risk of 'orphaned' sources), and plan for safe indefinite storage, license continuation, and property transaction complications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the agency disagrees widespread orphaning will occur given transition time, commenters must consider coordination with state/NRC authorities, indefinite secure storage responsibilities, license termination process impacts, and potential environmental review (NEPA) considerations if large-scale effects are plausible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of IAEA standards and domestic harmonization
rubrics_metrics.description: IAEA regulations are consensus, non-binding international standards; incorporation into U.S. regulations should be considered but may be adjusted domestically to account for risk-informed, performance-based U.S. regulatory approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOT will implement IAEA provisions 'to the extent practicable' and may deviate for cost/benefit, risk-informed decision-making, or domestic-only applications. Use rulemaking under 49 CFR 106 and APA processes to consider incorporation or domestic departures. Provide rationales when diverging from IAEA (e.g., TI multiplication factor for large dimension loads remains under analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recertification/approval process for new package designs
rubrics_metrics.description: New package designs (e.g., 20WC replacements) must undergo design, testing, licensing/CoC approval processes; anticipate design/testing/licensing costs and timelines when projecting impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume per-design costs in the hundreds of thousands (NRC typical estimates $300,000–$390,000) for design/testing/licensing and per-unit manufacturing/depreciation costs (examples given: manufacturing $50,000/package; depreciation $30,000/package). Use conservative estimates of number of designs and units when assessing industry-wide economic impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of import-first usage requirement for foreign Type A packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate the NPRM wording that required foreign-made Type A packaging to have been used for import of Class 7 materials before use in domestic/export shipments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign Type A packaging that meets IAEA standards may be used for domestic or export shipments without prior import use. Remove unnecessary barriers inconsistent with harmonization goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of transport index (TI) multiplication factors for large dimension loads
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether to include IAEA guidance on multiplication factors for transport index for large-dimension loads in U.S. regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize domestic variations from IAEA (e.g., communications, placarding) arise from cost/benefit and risk-informed analysis. Continue analysis to determine if TI multiplication factor should become a U.S. requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of historical testing not sufficient without contemporary QA
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical drop, fire and immersion tests (e.g., Sandia 1968) do not negate the need for contemporary QA programs, testing to international consensus standards, and stand-alone safety analysis reports for continued authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with prior testing, absence of QA elements and contemporary testing implies the package should be considered outdated/obsolete unless recertified to modern standards. Use contemporary consensus performance criteria to assess fitness for continued use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limits for comment consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comments outside the scope of the specific rulemaking will not be considered in the final rule deliberations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions or broad policy demands (e.g., recall of all released radioactive materials, policy reversals unrelated to the transport rule) are acknowledged but may be dismissed as out-of-scope for the subject rulemaking. Keep comments focused on the regulatory text, impacts, and technical standards being amended.
